_readme: Each command matches spoken phrases (fuzzy-matched) to keyboard actions sent to Star Citizen. Entries marked 'verified': false use my best-known DEFAULT Star Citizen keybinds and are NOT guaranteed current for your patch/HOTAS setup. Test each one in a safe spot (Arena Commander or docked at a station) and fix the 'keys' field in this file if it doesn't match what's in your Options > Keybindings screen. Key names follow the pydirectinput/win32 naming: single letters, 'f1'-'f12', 'space', 'enter', 'down', 'esc', etc.  Each command also carries display_name / category / key_label, which are what the printable Voice Command Reference is generated from -- run tools/make_reference.py after editing so the poster cannot drift.

settings._voice_pack_note: Name of a subfolder inside voice_acks/ to use for spoken acknowledgements. Empty = the built-in voice. A pack is just a folder of <command_id>.wav files -- drop one in and name it here.
settings._fallback_tts_note: true = commands with no recorded clip are read out by the built-in robot voice. false = they stay silent until a real clip exists. Set a single command to never speak with "silent": true on that command.
settings._control_scheme_note: Which file in config/schemes/ decides what each command actually presses. Copy keyboard_default.json, edit the keys to match YOUR layout, and name it here -- your spoken phrases never change.

commands.notes: F1 has been the mobiGlas toggle across many patches. Still double check.
Same toggle key as open.

User-confirmed key: R alone. Used with a destination already searched/highlighted on the map (e.g. via GameGlass or manual click) -- this just confirms the route. The auto-type-destination version (set_route) was removed by request; this is the only route command now.
F2 toggles the starmap, so one command carries both wordings. Do NOT add a separate close command: it duplicates these phrases and the two score identically, so the wrong one can win.

commands.notes: Hold Mouse Button 1. Confirmed against Star Citizen's own defaultProfile.xml: v_toggle_qdrive_engagement has keyboard='mouse1'. hold_ms raised 1500 -> 3000 by Obly on 2026-08-21; the original 1500 was an untested guess flagged in the README, this is his tuned value. Needs a target already selected. Deliberately does NOT touch NAV mode -- see the nav_mode command -- because that key is a toggle and could flip the wrong way if already in NAV. DESIGN DECISION: the hold blocks the command loop for its full duration; accepted, same as boost / autoland / spacebrake.

User-confirmed key: hold B, described as 'a long hold'. hold_ms=2000 is a guess at how long -- watch in-game whether it actually triggers the switch and tune. This is a TOGGLE (SCM<->NAV), not a direct select, so saying it twice in a row flips back. Hold time normalised into Obly's 3-5 second band on 2026-08-21.
User-confirmed key: N. Matches the current default per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, checked 2026-08-15).

Holds N (as in Nancy) for 6000 ms -- set by Obly on 2026-08-21, up from 2500 ms, because autoland needs the key held longer than five seconds to take. Confirmed against Star Citizen's own defaultProfile.xml: v_autoland defaults to 'n' with activationMode 'delayed_press', i.e. the game deliberately requires a long hold, which is what separates it from landing_gear (same key, tap). DESIGN DECISION (Obly, 2026-08-21): the hold blocks the command loop for its full duration, so no other voice command can fire while it runs. Accepted deliberately -- the in-game action takes that long anyway, so there is nothing useful to say mid-action. Do not 'fix' this by moving holds to a background thread without asking; it was raised and declined.
User-confirmed key: K. Matches the current default per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, checked 2026-08-15).

Phrases require the word 'toggle' or 'on'/'off' so this doesn't collide with raise_power_engines / lower_power_engines / full_power_engines. Matches the current default per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, checked 2026-08-15).

commands.notes: User-confirmed: F7 + Left Alt to nudge shield power pip down one step. KNOWN ISSUE (2026-08-15): user reported it drops several pips instead of one. Suspected cause: Star Citizen's power pips may shift continuously while the key is held (not a single discrete step per tap), and this script's default ~50ms hold may be long enough to register multiple ticks. Candidate fix, not yet applied: shorten the hold duration (near-instant tap) via a lower hold_ms on the keypress. User said this is fine to leave for now. Matches the current default per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, checked 2026-08-15).

User-confirmed key: L. This is a single toggle key, not separate on/off binds -- every phrase here just flips current state. If Star Citizen has a distinct 'lights on' vs 'lights off' bind, tell me and this can be split into two real commands instead. Matches the current default per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, checked 2026-08-15).

User-confirmed: Right Alt + R. This is the standalone 'turn everything on' phrasing -- see park_ship for the 'turn everything off' macro sharing this same key. Matches the current default per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, checked 2026-08-15).

Two-step macro per user description: cut thruster power, then toggle Flight Ready off. Uses the same Right Alt+R key as toggle_flight_ready, so this only makes sense to say while flight-ready is currently ON.

Bound to '/' (main-row slash, pydirectinput scancode 0x35) at Obly's direction, 2026-08-21. IMPORTANT: Star Citizen ships NO default keybind for any door action -- confirmed from the game's own defaultProfile.xml, where v_toggle_all_doors / v_open_all_doors / v_close_all_doors all have keyboard=''. So sending '/' only does something once the player has ALSO bound '/' to 'Toggle All Doors' inside Star Citizen's own keybindings. This is a suggested default, not a game default. If the player binds the action to a different key, sc_keybinds.py reads their actionmaps.xml and sends their key instead.

Right Alt + '/' at Obly's direction, 2026-08-21. Star Citizen ships NO default for v_toggle_all_doorlocks (keyboard='' in defaultProfile.xml), so this only does something once the player has also bound Right Alt + / to 'Toggle All Door Locks' in game. Distinct from toggle_port_locks (ralt+K), which IS a game default.

Standalone 'cut everything' command, distinct from park_ship. Uses U (Toggle Power - All) per a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-15) -- NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game yet. U is a TOGGLE, so saying this again while already powered down will turn things back ON, not keep them off. Bare 'power down' moved here from park_ship (2026-08-16) to avoid a duplicate-phrase collision. 'power down the ship' / 'shut down the ship' also moved here from park_ship (2026-08-16, user request) -- park_ship now only handles 'park ship' / 'we're parked'. The headlights (L) step that used to run alongside U was removed by user request (2026-08-16) -- this command now sends U alone; if Power-All doesn't cover exterior lights, headlights will need a separate 'lights off' command.

CORRECTED (2026-08-16, user instruction): key changed from Right Alt+H to Left Alt+H -- user confirmed Left Alt+H is the real toggle-helmet bind in-game. Right Alt+H is now reserved for the new 'present' macro command below (helmet + stand). Single TOGGLE key, not separate on/off binds (same pattern as headlights) -- every phrase here just flips current state, so saying 'remove helmet' while it's already off puts it back on. VOICE ACK REMOVED (2026-08-19, user request -- personal preference, silent by default): ack left empty on purpose, voice_acks/toggle_helmet.wav deleted.
ADDED 2026-08-16 per user instruction: 'present' holds the helmet (Right Alt+H) and stands up (hold Y ~6s, same hold-to-exit-seat behavior as the exit_seat command) in one voice command.

HIGH-STAKES COMMAND -- destroys the ship if it works as intended. Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-16): 'Self Destruct' = Backspace, Vehicles-Cockpit category. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game. hold_ms=3000 is a GUESS -- the source didn't document whether this needs a tap or a hold, but self-destruct actions in most games require a multi-second hold specifically to prevent accidental activation, so a hold was the safer assumption. Phrase list deliberately kept more conservative than other commands per user request (2026-08-16): explicitly rejected 'abandon ship'; did not include 'blow it up' (too generic) or 'boom'/'kaboom' (too short/casual, high false-trigger risk for a command with this consequence) since the user didn't confirm them. Test this one with extreme caution -- confirm the actual key and hold duration in a context where losing the ship doesn't matter (e.g. freshly spawned, no cargo/insurance concerns) before trusting it. DESIGN DECISION (Obly, 2026-08-21): deliberately NOT marked strict. Raised twice -- single-word trigger, expensive if misheard -- and declined both times. He wants it to fire on one word. Do not add strict/match_threshold to this command without asking.

CORRECTED (2026-08-16, user report): this is a HOLD, not a tap -- user specified longer than 3-5 seconds, so hold_ms=6000 to clearly clear that bar. Originally built as a tap based on the community keybind reference (nomans.space) not specifying hold vs press; that reference's key itself (Y, with the source's own table showing Z due to a British/QWERTZ-layout documentation quirk) is still unconfirmed, only the tap-vs-hold behavior has now been corrected. A separate 'Emergency Exit Seat' action exists (U + Left Shift, a faster/forced eject variant) but was not added -- ask the user if they want that as its own command too. VOICE ACK REMOVED (2026-08-19, user request): no spoken response for this command anymore -- ack left empty on purpose (main.py's speak() is skipped entirely when ack is empty), and voice_acks/exit_seat.wav was deleted. Hold time normalised into Obly's 3-5 second band on 2026-08-21.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-16): 'Hail Target' = 9, Flight - Target Hailing category. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game. Deliberately kept 'contact'-style phrasing (e.g. 'contact target') OUT of this list -- request_landing already owns 'contact tower' / 'contact atc' / 'contact station', and 'contact' alone is ambiguous between the two; stuck to 'hail' wording to keep them distinct.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Activate Ping' = Tab, Flight - Radar category, listed as a Hold & Release action (not a tap) -- charge strength/range scales with hold duration in-game. hold_ms=1500 is a starting guess at a solid mid-strength ping; tune once tested. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game. Hold time normalised into Obly's 3-5 second band on 2026-08-21.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Emergency Exit Seat' = U + Left Shift, Vehicles - Seats and Operator Modes category. The fast/forced variant of exit_seat -- that one is a 6-second hold on Y, this is a quick tap on a completely different key combo. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Eject' = Right Alt + Y, Vehicles - Seats and Operator Modes category. Distinct from both exit_seat and emergency_exit_seat -- this ejects you from the ship entirely rather than just leaving your seat. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game. HIGH-STAKES-ish like self_destruct in spirit (you leave the ship mid-flight) -- test somewhere it doesn't matter first. DESIGN DECISION (Obly, 2026-08-21): deliberately NOT marked strict. Raised twice -- single-word trigger, expensive if misheard -- and declined both times. He wants it to fire on one word. Do not add strict/match_threshold to this command without asking.

Left Shift, hold-to-boost (not a toggle). hold_ms=5000 set by Obly on 2026-08-21, replacing the 1500 ms guess. Confirmed against Star Citizen's own defaultProfile.xml: v_afterburner defaults to lshift with activationMode 'all', i.e. it boosts for as long as the key is held, so a longer hold simply means a longer burn. DESIGN DECISION (Obly, 2026-08-21): the hold blocks the command loop for its full duration, so no other voice command can fire while it runs. Accepted deliberately -- the in-game action takes that long anyway, so there is nothing useful to say mid-action. Do not 'fix' this by moving holds to a background thread without asking; it was raised and declined.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Decoupled Mode' = C (Toggle, Hold), Flight - Movement category. Listed as both toggle-capable and hold-capable in-game; implemented here as a simple tap/toggle. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

X = space brake, Flight-Movement. Changed from a tap to a 5000 ms HOLD by Obly on 2026-08-21. Star Citizen's own defaultProfile.xml has v_space_brake on 'x' with no tap activationMode, i.e. it brakes for as long as the key is held, so a hold is the correct shape for this action and a tap barely did anything. DESIGN DECISION: the hold blocks the command loop for its full duration -- accepted, same as boost and autoland, because the in-game action takes that long anyway.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Toggle Scanning Operator Mode' = V, Vehicles - Seats and Operator Modes category. Pairs naturally with the ping command above. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Toggle Mining Operator Mode' = M, Vehicles - Seats and Operator Modes category. Same physical key as toggle_salvage_mode below -- the game resolves which mode actually applies based on what your current ship supports, same pattern as other shared-key commands across this whole project series. Only useful in a mining-capable ship. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Toggle Salvage Operator Mode' = M, Vehicles - Seats and Operator Modes category. Same physical key as toggle_mining_mode above -- context-resolved by the game based on ship type. Only useful in a salvage-capable ship. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Next Operator Mode' = Mouse Button 3 (middle click), Vehicles - Seats and Operator Modes category. Sent as a short mousehold to act like a click. Cycles between whatever operator modes your current ship actually supports. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Request Cargo Loading' = Right Alt + N, Flight - Movement category. Same family as request_landing (Left Alt + N) but a distinct action. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

Sourced from a community keybind reference (nomans.space, 2026-08-19): 'Cycle camera view' = F4, Vehicles - View category. Cycles First Person -> Third Person -> Director Mode. Replaces the originally-suggested 'Look Behind' (Comma) per user request (2026-08-19) -- that one was dropped, this is what shipped instead. Deliberately did not add a bare 'view' phrase -- too generic, real risk of false-triggering on unrelated speech containing that common word. NOT personally confirmed by the user in-game.

User-confirmed key: F -- Star Citizen's standard universal interact/use key (also matches the general on-foot keybind reference checked early this session). NOT yet live-tested with this specific command.

Right Alt + K. This one is a REAL Star Citizen default, not a suggestion: the game's own defaultProfile.xml has v_toggle_all_portlocks with keyboard='ralt+K' in both spaceship_general and vehicle_general. Separate action from the door locks (v_toggle_all_doorlocks), which has no default. Phrases are deliberately port-first: 'lock all ports' was removed because it differs from the door command's 'lock all doors' by a single word and invited a misfire. No Raina voice clip exists for this command yet, so the ack falls back to the Windows TTS voice until one is generated.

Left Alt + X. A REAL Star Citizen default, confirmed from the game's own defaultProfile.xml: action 'visor_wipe' with keyboard='lalt+x', UILabel @ui_CIHelmetVisorWipe, present in spaceship_hud, vehicle_general and player actionmaps. Note it is LEFT alt, not right. Works without the player binding anything. No Raina voice clip yet, so the ack falls back to Windows TTS.

Right mouse button held 5000 ms, per Obly 2026-08-21. FLAG -- this does NOT match Star Citizen's default. The game's own defaultProfile.xml has v_toggle_jump_request (@ui_CIJumpDriveJumpRequest) on mouse='mouse1' with activationMode='tap' -- LEFT click, tapped. And mouse2 (right click) defaults to v_ads_toggle, so on a stock install this command would toggle aim-down-sights instead of jumping. Obly's own actionmaps.xml has v_toggle_jump_request on js1_button2 (stick), so neither mouse button is his live binding either. Confirm before shipping to testers. Phrase list deliberately kept to the full 'activate jump point' at Obly's direction 2026-08-21. Bare 'jump point' was removed because this sends a 5-second right-click hold, and right-click on foot maps to throw_underhand -- saying it accidentally while holding a grenade throws it. Three deliberate words is not something Whisper produces by accident; two words is.

Pastes the destination into the map's search box and presses Enter -- that is all. Say 'open map' first and 'set route' after; each command does one thing, so a mis-heard word never toggles the map shut. The spoken name is corrected against config/places.json before it is pasted, so 'laura ville' becomes 'Lorville'. UNVERIFIED in-game: walk it through docked once and correct the keys.
Searches everything the program knows -- places, ships, commodities and shops -- and reads back what it finds. Sends no keys to the game, so it is safe to use any time, focused or not.
